conditions.name: cellulitis
conditions.description: Bacterial infection spreading through soft tissue. The site grows hot, red, and tender.

conditions.name: acute radiation sickness
conditions.description: Symptoms of high-dose radiation exposure. Mild doses cause nausea and fatigue; severe doses produce spontaneous bleeding as the body's blood-forming tissues fail.

stages.description: Early symptoms of radiation exposure — nausea and fatigue from a low-grade dose.
Moderate radiation exposure — repeated vomiting, hair loss, and visible bruising as bone marrow function falters.
Severe radiation exposure — multi-system failure approaches. Bone marrow function has effectively stopped; spontaneous bleeding follows.

conditions.name: chronic radiation accumulation
conditions.description: Accumulated radiation dose from sustained exposure. Slow to clear and subtle in presentation — vague fatigue, mild GI complaints.

conditions.name: toxic poisoning
conditions.description: Toxins in the bloodstream exceed what the liver can clear. The patient looks sick — jaundiced, nauseous, lethargic.

conditions.name: tissue hypoxia
conditions.description: Oxygen demand exceeds delivery at the tissue level. Patients turn pale and dusky, breathing labored, mental status dulled. Resolved by treating the underlying cause and oxygenating.

conditions.name: hypothermia
conditions.description: Core body temperature has dropped well below normal. Shivering, slowed movement, confusion.

conditions.name: heatstroke
conditions.description: Core body temperature has risen well above normal. Flushed skin, confusion, and weakness.

conditions.name: genetic damage
conditions.description: Damage at the cellular level — DNA strands disrupted by radiation, cloning errors, or other catalytic insult. Outwardly subtle; treated with ryetalyn.

conditions.name: radiation burns
conditions.description: Deep erythema, blistering and moist desquamation over a limb, without any history of heat or flame — the skin was killed from within by an extreme radiation dose. Painful and slow to heal; treat as a burn while the dose is cleared.

conditions.name: radiation poisoning
conditions.description: Blood toxicity from widespread radiation-induced cell death. Nausea, vomiting, weakness and pallor that persist until the dose is purged. Antitoxins clear the debris; anti-radiation drugs stop more from forming.

conditions.name: cohesion loss
conditions.description: Trauma has torn the bonds between the swarm's nanites. The body moves sluggishly, holds tools poorly and tears more easily under further blows. The swarm reknits itself from refactory steel (regeneration) or with nanopaste; without steel it keeps unravelling.

effects: Physical injury taken: +29% at full severity

conditions.name: refactory depletion
conditions.description: The refactory has run out of steel while the swarm needed repair. The nanites cannibalise one another to stay whole: regeneration slows and the body grows sluggish. Feed the refactory steel.

conditions.name: orchestrator damage
conditions.description: The orchestrator module, which coordinates the swarm, is damaged. Movement and aim lose precision, form changes can fail outright, and at worst the swarm loses awareness. Recalibrate it with a multitool or reboot programmer and repair its wiring.

conditions.name: swarm contamination
conditions.description: Foreign reagents or materials have worked their way into the swarm and the refactory. The nanites misfire around the contaminant: healing slows and fine control suffers. Purge the reagents; the refactory filters the rest while the swarm regenerates.

conditions.name: form strain
conditions.description: The swarm has been reshaped too quickly, or held in a shapeless form too long, and its structure is fatigued. Movement and attacks slow. It eases with rest in humanoid form, recalibration or regeneration.

conditions.name: flux sickness
conditions.description: Exposure to an unstable, reality-bending energy field. Cells replicate erratically and the blood fills with metabolic debris. Presents like mild radiation sickness with a characteristic metallic taste and flickering vision. Antitoxins clear the debris; genetic repair reverses the cellular damage.

conditions.name: profane corruption
conditions.description: An unidentifiable contaminant saturating the blood and nervous system, accompanied by fever, auditory hallucinations and a pervasive sense of dread. It recedes slowly on its own once the source is removed; antitoxins hasten it.

conditions.name: hepatic failure
conditions.description: The liver can no longer clear metabolites or regulate clotting. Toxins accumulate in the bloodstream.

conditions.name: renal failure
conditions.description: The kidneys have stopped clearing waste. Electrolytes drift and fluid balance fails.

conditions.name: ischemic vision loss
conditions.description: Loss of vision from the eyes being starved of blood for too long. Without rapid restoration of circulation, the loss becomes permanent.

conditions.name: heart damage
conditions.description: Injury to the heart itself. As the pump's output falls, perfusion suffers; when pump function collapses outright, cardiac arrest follows.

stages.name: cardiogenic shock
stages.description: The heart is failing to pump effectively. Tissue perfusion drops despite adequate blood volume.

stages.name: decompensated heart failure
stages.description: The failing heart muscle can no longer hold a rhythm: it fibrillates into cardiac arrest (see cardiac arrhythmia). Without intervention, irreversible brain injury follows within minutes.

conditions.name: brain damage
conditions.description: Injury to brain tissue. Mild loss of cognition starts well before severe neurological collapse; advanced damage threatens herniation. Once tissue damage crosses the salvageable threshold, the brain decays faster than chemistry can repair it. No surgery reverses established brain damage.

stages.name: anoxic brain injury
stages.description: Brain tissue starved of oxygen long enough to show neurological deficits — confusion, slowed cognition, impaired vision. Alkysine can repair the underlying damage.

stages.name: brain herniation
stages.description: Cranial pressure has displaced brain tissue past the structures that contain it. Past this point, neurological function does not return.

conditions.name: pulmonary contusion
conditions.description: Bruised lung tissue from a heavy chest impact. Breathing grows harder as fluid accumulates in the lung.

conditions.name: respiratory failure
conditions.description: The lungs can no longer oxygenate the blood. Without oxygen the rest of the body begins to suffocate from the inside.

conditions.name: arithrazine toxicity

conditions.name: alkysine confusion

conditions.name: tramadol overdose

conditions.name: paracetamol overdose

conditions.name: menthol overdose

conditions.name: dexalin overdose
conditions.description: Excess dexalin disrupts normal oxygen exchange — paradoxically, too much makes breathing less effective.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: dexalin-plus overdose
conditions.description: Dexalin-plus at overdose causes the same paradoxical oxygenation failure as dexalin, but at higher intensity, with confusion and motor symptoms.

conditions.name: inaprovaline overdose
conditions.description: Excess inaprovaline depresses cardiac output. Hypotension, bradycardia, and reduced respiratory drive.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: norepinephrine overdose

conditions.name: leporazine overdose

conditions.name: corophizine overdose

conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: antitoxin overdose
conditions.description: Antitoxin at overdose disrupts the body's normal electrolyte balance. Patients become weak, nauseated, and disoriented.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: carthatoline overdose
conditions.description: Carthatoline at overdose strips the patient's electrolytes alongside the toxins it's meant to clear. Dehydration, weakness, and ongoing GI distress.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: hyronalin overdose
conditions.description: Hyronalin overdose stresses the same tissues it's meant to protect — patients feel weak and queasy.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: arithrazine overdose
conditions.description: Arithrazine at overdose is severely tissue-damaging — the same reactivity that scrubs radiation out of the cellular machinery turns indiscriminate. Persistent tox loading, weakness, and broad organ stress.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: calcium carbonate overdose
conditions.description: Excess calcium carbonate overwhelms the gut — chalky residue irritates the stomach lining, throws off electrolytes, and the kidneys strain to clear the load. Nausea and abdominal tenderness predominate.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: ethylredoxrazine overdose

conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: immunosuprizine overdose
conditions.description: Immunosuprizine at overdose strips the immune response beyond its therapeutic window — patients become fragile to incidental infection, with rising toxin load as cellular byproducts go uncleared. The trade-off: organ rejection is held off even more aggressively, useful when a fresh transplant is teetering.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: stimulant overdose
conditions.description: Hyperzine at overdose drives the heart and adrenergic system past their working range. Severe tachycardia, hypertension, toxic muscle stress. Patients in this state move noticeably faster and shrug off pain — combat use is a known abuse, but the heart strain and toxin damage are real.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: alkysine overdose
conditions.description: Excess alkysine is itself neurotoxic — the same neurotransmitter pathway it's meant to support gets overwhelmed. Confusion, headache, and accumulating brain damage.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: synaptizine overdose
conditions.description: Synaptizine at overdose drives the CNS past stimulation into excitotoxicity — restless tremor, accelerated heart rate, tissue stress on the brain. The chem also crosses the blood-brain barrier hard enough at OD doses to repair tissue damage above the salvage threshold — but only enough to win if paired with alkysine. Past the terminal threshold, brain decay outpaces any combination.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: earthsblood overdose
conditions.description: Earthsblood's psychoactive component overwhelms the cortex at overdose — the same neuron-tithing that powers its healing turns aggressive. Hallucinations, confusion, and ongoing brain tissue loss. The hand-off it offers in exchange: tox, oxy, and clone damage continue to bleed off rapidly even at OD.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: peridaxon overdose
conditions.description: Peridaxon at overdose induces hallucinations and disorientation — the same organ-receptor priming that makes it useful at therapeutic dose becomes overwhelming at high concentrations.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: imidazoline overdose
conditions.description: Imidazoline at overdose paradoxically blurs vision and irritates the retina — too much of the receptor agonist overwhelms the normal signal.

conditions.name: osteodaxon overdose

conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: respirodaxon overdose
conditions.description: Respirodaxon overdose over-proliferates lung tissue, paradoxically reducing gas exchange efficiency.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: cordradaxon overdose

conditions.name: hepanephrodaxon overdose

conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: gastirodaxon overdose
conditions.description: Gastirodaxon overdose causes inflammatory GI cramping and impaired absorption.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: rezadone overdose
conditions.description: Rezadone at overdose causes uncontrolled cellular replication — disorientation, weakness, and minor toxic effects as the body struggles to keep up.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: ryetalyn overdose
conditions.description: Ryetalyn at overdose interferes with normal cellular processes outside the genetic targets it's meant to fix. Weakness and mild GI symptoms.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: spaceacillin overdose
conditions.description: Spaceacillin overdose produces broad GI disturbance and mild liver stress.
conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: bicaridine overdose
conditions.description: Bicaridine at overdose interferes with normal clotting — the patient becomes prone to spontaneous bleeding. The same antiplatelet activity also drains intracranial bleeding faster than any other chem can; a bicaridine OD will resolve a subdural hematoma when no surgeon is available, at the cost of broad external bleeding.

conditions.name: bicaridaze overdose

conditions.progression: clears as the chem leaves the body

conditions.name: kelotane overdose

conditions.name: dermaline overdose

conditions.name: tricordrazine overdose

conditions.name: myelamine overdose

conditions.description: If left untreated, subject will become a xenochimera upon perishing.

effects: Heart rate: +15 bpm at full severity

conditions.name: acute pain
conditions.description: Overwhelming pain from a stunning blow, shock weapon or similar insult. Fades quickly on its own; painkillers speed recovery.

conditions.name: core dormancy
conditions.description: The nanite swarm has lost cohesion and retreated into its control core. The core must be opened, recalibrated with a reboot programmer, rebuilt with nanopaste and jump-started with a defibrillator.

conditions.name: lacerated artery
conditions.description: A torn artery in a limb. Blood loss is rapid and obvious; direct pressure or a tourniquet is the only way to stop it.

conditions.name: severed tendon
conditions.description: A cut tendon. The limb won't move properly until it's surgically reattached — medicines won't fix it.

conditions.name: nerve damage
conditions.description: Peripheral nerves injured by trauma, crushing, or heat. Sensation in the affected limb is partly lost and returns slowly on its own.

conditions.name: compartment syndrome
conditions.description: Swelling inside a limb has cut off its own blood supply. Untreated, the tissue inside dies.

conditions.name: tissue necrosis
conditions.description: Dead tissue in a limb. It does not recover; surgical removal is the only way to stop it from poisoning the rest of the body.

conditions.name: deep bruising
conditions.description: Bruised soft tissue from a heavy impact. Sore, but the body heals it on its own given time.

effects: Heart rate: +8 bpm at full severity

conditions.name: internal hemorrhage
conditions.description: Bleeding into the body cavity from torn vessels. Symptoms are often subtle until enough blood has been lost to start affecting circulation.

conditions.name: hypovolemic shock
conditions.description: Circulatory collapse from heavy blood loss. The body can no longer perfuse its tissues, and shock takes over.

conditions.name: untreated fracture
conditions.description: A bone broken and left unset. The surrounding tissue grinds against the fragments with every movement.

stages.name: untreated fracture
stages.description: A broken leg bone, unset and unsupported. Every step grinds the fragments.

stages.name: splinted fracture
stages.description: A broken leg bone held still by a splint.

stages.name: untreated fracture
stages.description: A broken arm bone, unset and unsupported.

stages.name: splinted fracture
stages.description: A broken arm bone held still by a splint.

stages.name: untreated fracture
stages.description: A broken bone, unset and unsupported.

stages.name: splinted fracture
stages.description: A broken bone held still by a splint.

conditions.name: concussion
conditions.description: A brief disruption of brain function from a blow to the head. The first one usually resolves on its own; a second on top of it is far more serious.

conditions.name: burn shock
conditions.description: Systemic shock following extensive thermal injury. The more of the body's surface is burned, the harder it gets to stabilise.

conditions.name: wound infection
conditions.description: Bacterial colonisation of an open wound. The dirtier the wound was when it was inflicted, the faster the infection takes hold.

conditions.name: airway obstruction
conditions.description: Something is lodged in the upper airway — food, aspirated vomit, blood or displaced tissue from facial trauma. A complete obstruction stops all gas exchange: the patient can't breathe, speak or cough. Abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich manoeuvre, help intent on the chest) or an airway kit clear it; a conscious patient may cough a partial one free.

effects: Blocked actions: set at full severity
Heart rate: +15 bpm at full severity

conditions.name: airway edema
conditions.description: The tissues of the throat and upper airway are swelling shut — an allergic reaction or an inhalation burn. Breathing grows noisy (stridor) and then stops altogether once the airway closes. A vasopressor (adrenaline; an AllergyPen's inaprovaline in a pinch) shrinks the swelling; an airway kit holds it open.

effects: Systolic pressure: -15 mmHg at full severity
Heart rate: +20 bpm at full severity

conditions.name: respiratory arrest
conditions.description: The drive to breathe has failed — an opioid overdose, brain herniation or profound hypoxia. The heart may still beat, but no breaths are taken. Someone must breathe for the patient: a bag-valve mask, or rescue breaths during CPR. The drive returns once its cause is treated.

effects: Heart rate: +10 bpm at full severity

conditions.name: pneumothorax
conditions.description: Air has leaked into the chest cavity and is collapsing the lung. Left alone the pressure builds into a tension pneumothorax that crushes the heart's return and stops gas exchange. A decompression needle vents it in the field; a chest tube is definitive. If the lung itself is perforated, air keeps leaking back in until the hole is surgically repaired.

stages.name: pneumothorax
stages.description: A partially collapsed lung. Breath sounds are quiet on the affected side.

stages.name: tension pneumothorax
stages.description: Trapped air under pressure has shoved the trachea aside and is crushing the heart's venous return. Decompress now.

conditions.name: cardiac arrhythmia
conditions.description: The heart's electrical rhythm has broken down. A fast unstable rhythm still pumps but degenerates if untreated. Ventricular fibrillation (VF) and asystole pump nothing: the patient collapses, the brain starts dying within minutes, and only CPR buys time. A defibrillator converts VF but cannot restart a flatline — asystole needs CPR and a vasopressor (adrenaline) until it coarsens into a shockable rhythm.

stages.name: post-arrest rhythm
stages.description: The rhythm has been restored and is settling. Monitor; it resolves on its own.

stages.name: unstable tachyarrhythmia
stages.description: A fast, disorganised rhythm that still perfuses the body. Cardiac drugs settle it; stimulants push it over into VF.

stages.name: ventricular fibrillation
stages.description: The ventricles quiver without pumping. No pulse, no blood pressure. Shockable: defibrillate, and keep up CPR until the paddles are ready.

stages.name: asystole
stages.description: A flatline. No electrical activity to shock. CPR and a vasopressor may coarsen it into VF, which can then be shocked.

conditions.name: cytolytic toxaemia
conditions.description: A viral cytolysin is dissolving cell membranes throughout the body. Profound weakness, pallor and internal pressure; if the agent is not cleared the tissues eventually fail catastrophically.

conditions.name: limb ischemia
conditions.description: A limb cut off from its blood supply, usually by a tourniquet. The tissue starves while the flow is stopped; left too long, it dies and must be cut away. Restoring flow lets it recover.

conditions.name: gel dissolution
conditions.description: The patient's gelatinous body is dissolving in water. Dry them off; the gel recovers on its own once dry.

reagents.name: Kelotane
reagents.description: Kelotane is a drug used to treat burns.

overdose.description: Excess kelotane irritates the digestive tract. Nausea and tissue inflammation as the drug overwhelms the body's normal burn-response pathway.

reagents.name: Dermaline
reagents.description: Dermaline is the next step in burn medication. Works twice as good as kelotane and enables the body to restore even the direst heat-damaged tissue.

overdose.description: Dermaline's potency makes its overdose harsher than kelotane's. Severe nausea, vascular dilation, and broad tissue irritation.

reagents.name: Dermalaze
reagents.description: Dermalaze is a topical variant of the chemical Dermaline.

reagents.name: Restorative Nanites
reagents.description: Miniature medical robots that swiftly restore bodily damage.

reagents.name: Neo Kelotane
reagents.description: An advancement of kelotane that scars and breaks apart the user's flesh to remove the burnt tissue.

reagents.name: Quadcord
reagents.description: An experimental drug that is meant to further enhance tricord

reagents.name: Tricordrazine
reagents.description: Tricordrazine is a highly potent stimulant, originally derived from cordrazine. Can be used to treat a wide range of injuries.

overdose.description: Tricordrazine overdose is severely toxic — the broad-spectrum stabiliser becomes a broad-spectrum harm. Multi-system distress, liver damage, and weakness.

reagents.name: Tricorlidaze
reagents.description: Tricorlidaze is a topical gel produced with tricordrazine and sterilizine.

reagents.name: Peridaxon
reagents.description: Used to encourage recovery of internal organs and nervous systems. Medicate cautiously.

overdose.description: Peridaxon at overdose induces hallucinations and disorientation — the same organ-receptor priming that makes it useful at therapeutic dose becomes overwhelming at high concentrations.

interactions.name: potentiated organ repair
interactions.description: Peridaxon's generic organ-repair pathway primes tissue receptors so the targeted daxon-family drugs (cordradaxon, respirodaxon, hepanephrodaxon, gastirodaxon) work faster. A documented synergy.

reagents.name: Respirodaxon
reagents.description: Used to repair the tissue of the lungs and similar organs.

overdose.description: Respirodaxon overdose over-proliferates lung tissue, paradoxically reducing gas exchange efficiency.

reagents.name: Rezadone
reagents.description: A powder with almost magical properties, this substance can effectively treat genetic damage in humanoids, though excessive consumption has side effects.

overdose.description: Rezadone at overdose causes uncontrolled cellular replication — disorientation, weakness, and minor toxic effects as the body struggles to keep up.

reagents.name: Earthsblood
reagents.description: A rare plant extract with immense, almost magical healing capabilities. Induces a potent psychoactive state, damaging neurons with prolonged use.

overdose.description: Earthsblood's psychoactive component overwhelms the cortex at overdose — the same neuron-tithing that powers its healing turns aggressive. Hallucinations, confusion, and ongoing brain tissue loss. The hand-off it offers in exchange: tox, oxy, and clone damage continue to bleed off rapidly even at OD.

reagents.name: bullvalene
reagents.description: A catalytic chemical that can treat a wide variety of ailments at the cost of toxifying the host's body.

reagents.name: Living Agent
reagents.description: Fill the body with life, while making it more senstive to stimulus.

reagents.name: Liquid protean
reagents.description: This seems to be a small portion of a Protean creature, still slightly wiggling.

reagents.name: Bicaridine
reagents.description: Bicaridine is an analgesic medication and can be used to treat blunt trauma.

overdose.description: Bicaridine at overdose interferes with normal clotting — the patient becomes prone to spontaneous bleeding. The same antiplatelet activity also drains intracranial bleeding faster than any other chem can; a bicaridine OD will resolve a subdural hematoma when no surgeon is available, at the cost of broad external bleeding.

interactions.name: antibiotic interference
interactions.description: Bicaridine's antiplatelet activity interferes with spaceacillin absorption. Spaceacillin treats infections at 40% of its normal effectiveness while both are in the body.

reagents.name: Bicaridaze
reagents.description: Bicaridaze is a topical variant of the chemical Bicaridine.

overdose.description: Bicaridaze is a topical bicaridine that's absorbed slowly through the skin. At overdose the same antiplatelet effect as bicaridine itself surfaces — bleeding becomes harder to control — with the added burden of cumulative skin/dermal irritation from the carrier.

reagents.name: Synaptizine
reagents.description: Synaptizine is used to treat various diseases.

overdose.description: Synaptizine at overdose drives the CNS past stimulation into excitotoxicity — restless tremor, accelerated heart rate, tissue stress on the brain. The chem also crosses the blood-brain barrier hard enough at OD doses to repair tissue damage above the salvage threshold — but only enough to win if paired with alkysine. Past the terminal threshold, brain decay outpaces any combination.

side_effects.name: synaptizine jitteriness
side_effects.description: Synaptizine's neuro-stimulant component can produce restless movements and elevated heart rate at therapeutic dose. Resolves as the chem clears.

interactions.name: potentiated neurorepair
interactions.description: Synaptizine opens the blood-brain barrier slightly, letting alkysine reach more damaged neural tissue per dose. The chems work together better than apart.

reagents.name: Alkysine
reagents.description: Alkysine is a drug used to lessen the damage to neurological tissue after a catastrophic injury. Can heal brain tissue.

overdose.description: Excess alkysine is itself neurotoxic — the same neurotransmitter pathway it's meant to support gets overwhelmed. Confusion, headache, and accumulating brain damage.

side_effects.name: alkysine confusion
side_effects.description: Alkysine in the bloodstream at therapeutic dose can produce mild confusion. Resolves as the chem clears.

interactions.name: potentiated neurorepair
interactions.description: Synaptizine opens the blood-brain barrier slightly, letting alkysine reach more damaged neural tissue per dose. The chems work together better than apart.

reagents.name: Myelamine
reagents.description: Used to rapidly clot hemorrhages by increasing the effectiveness of platelets. An ideal dosage of 10 units will fully heal any internal hemorrhages.

overdose.description: Myelamine at overdose drives clotting past the point of utility — platelets aggregate in the small vessels, creating microthrombi while the liver works overtime clearing the breakdown products. Chest pain, fatigue, and accumulating toxin damage.

reagents.name: Hannoa
reagents.description: A powerful clotting agent that treats brute damage very quickly but takes a long time to be metabolised. Overdoses easily, reacts badly with other chemicals.

overdose.description: Hannoa is a sap-derived clotting agent that metabolises very slowly, so it overdoses easily. Past the threshold its clotting runs away inside the vessels: the veins feel as if they are fusing shut, breathing becomes laboured, and the patient takes blunt tissue damage while wounds keep closing.

reagents.name: Spaceacillin
reagents.description: An all-purpose antiviral agent.

overdose.description: Spaceacillin overdose produces broad GI disturbance and mild liver stress.

causes.name: Blunt impact to the torso
causes.description: A heavy strike to the chest or abdomen — a fall, a thrown object, a body blow. Bruising forms beneath the skin; a hard enough impact can bruise the lung underneath.

causes.name: Blunt impact to the head
causes.description: A strike to the head. The first impact tends to concussion; a second on top of an existing concussion produces a far more serious subdural hematoma.

causes.name: Sharp injury to the torso
causes.description: A cut or piercing wound to the chest or abdomen — knife, gunshot, jagged metal. Internal bleeding is common; deep wounds can pierce the pleural cavity.

causes.name: Sharp injury to a limb
causes.description: A cut to an arm or leg. Shallow cuts risk tendon or nerve disruption; deeper ones can sever an artery and bleed dangerously fast.

causes.name: Burn injury to the head or face
causes.description: Heat or chemical injury to the face and airway. The upper airway swells and gas exchange suffers.

causes.name: Extensive body burns
causes.description: Burns spread across enough of the body that fluid balance fails and systemic shock sets in.

causes.name: Severe limb burns
causes.description: Deep burns to a limb cause swelling within the muscle compartment. Pressure builds and tissue suffocates.

causes.name: Breach of a synthetic torso
causes.description: A cut or puncture through chassis plating — the coolant loop and power bus run just beneath.

causes.name: Burn through a synthetic torso
causes.description: Heat or current through the chassis fuses power distribution.

causes.name: Impact to a synthetic limb
causes.description: A hard knock to a prosthetic limb throws its actuators out of calibration.

causes.name: Impact to a synthetic head
causes.description: A blow to the processor housing corrupts memory and processing.

causes.name: Brain damage
causes.description: Injury to the brain itself. Mild loss of cognition starts well before severe neurological collapse, and pressure-driven herniation is the end of the line.

causes.name: Heart damage
causes.description: Injury to the heart itself. As pump output falls, perfusion suffers; once the pump fails outright, cardiac arrest follows.

causes.name: Lung damage
causes.description: Injury to the lungs themselves. Once they can no longer move enough air, hypoxia spreads to every other organ.

causes.name: Liver damage
causes.description: Injury to the liver itself. Past the point of function it can no longer clear metabolites, and toxins accumulate in the bloodstream.

causes.name: Kidney damage
causes.description: Injury to the kidneys themselves. They stop clearing waste; electrolytes drift and fluid balance fails.

causes.name: Eye damage
causes.description: Injury to the eyes themselves — through hypoperfusion or direct trauma — producing blurred or absent vision.

causes.name: Untreated deep bruising
causes.description: Bruising left untreated can deepen into a true internal bleed as the damaged vessels fail.

causes.name: Sustained internal hemorrhage
causes.description: Once enough blood has been lost, the body can no longer compensate. Circulation collapses into hypovolemic shock.

causes.name: Untreated arterial bleed
causes.description: Continued blood loss from a torn artery progresses to hypovolemic shock if not stopped.

causes.name: Deepening inhalation burn
causes.description: A scorched airway swells. Past a point the swelling closes the throat entirely.

causes.name: Profound hypoxia
causes.description: A brainstem starved of oxygen stops driving breathing. The patient stops breathing on their own.

causes.name: Hypoxic cardiac arrest
causes.description: A heart starved of oxygen fibrillates and stops pumping.

causes.name: Severe burn shock
causes.description: Heavy burns cause massive fluid loss through damaged skin, driving the patient into hypovolemic shock.

causes.name: Long-untreated fracture
causes.description: An unset fracture eventually invites infection at the wound site.

causes.name: Untreated compartment syndrome
causes.description: Tissue starved of blood inside a swollen compartment eventually dies. The dead tissue must be removed surgically.

causes.name: Spreading wound infection
causes.description: Bacteria escape the wound site and spread through the surrounding soft tissue.

causes.name: Cellulitis breaching the bloodstream
causes.description: Once cellulitis seeds infection into the bloodstream, the whole body's inflammatory response activates: sepsis.

causes.name: Decompensated sepsis
causes.description: Sepsis past the point of compensation: blood pressure collapses despite reflexive tachycardia. Septic shock.

causes.name: Wound contamination
causes.description: Once the bacteria load on a wound passes a threshold, a wound infection forms there.

causes.name: Acute radiation exposure
causes.description: A high single dose of ionising radiation. Mild doses cause nausea and fatigue; severe doses cause spontaneous bleeding and organ failure.

causes.name: Chronic radiation dose
causes.description: Sustained or accumulated radiation exposure over time. Persists after acute symptoms have cleared; clears slowly without treatment.

causes.name: Cold exposure
causes.description: Body temperature has dropped well below normal. Cold environments, lack of insulation, or shock can cause it.

causes.name: Heat exposure
causes.description: Body temperature has risen well above normal. Hot environments, fevers, or burns can drive it.

causes.name: Contagion exposure
causes.description: An infectious agent passed from a carrier: through the air, by touch or through blood. Protective clothing, masks and internals block exposure; a body that has beaten a strain before is immune to it.

surgeries.name: Fracture setting
surgeries.description: Re-aligning a broken bone and securing it with bone gel or a setter so it can heal cleanly.
steps: Cut through the skin and muscle over the fracture.
Clamp any bleeding vessels at the wound edge.
Retract the skin to expose the bone.
Set the bone with a bone setter or bone gel.
Cauterize the incision closed.

surgeries.name: Vessel repair
surgeries.description: Locating and repairing a torn vessel. Stops arterial and internal bleeding that pressure alone can't control.
steps: Cut down through the tissue overlying the bleed.
Clamp the bleeders and retract the tissue.
Mend the vessel wall with a FixOVein.
Cauterize the incision closed.

surgeries.name: Tendon repair
surgeries.description: Locating, freeing and rejoining a severed tendon so the limb regains function.
steps: Cut down to expose the severed tendon.
Retract the tissue around it.
Bring the tendon ends together and join them.
Cauterize the incision closed.

surgeries.name: Debridement
surgeries.description: Cutting away dead or badly infected tissue so the healthy tissue around it can recover. The only treatment for necrosis.
steps: Open the skin over the affected tissue.
Retract the wound edges.
Cut away the dead and infected tissue.
Cauterize the wound closed.

surgeries.name: Fasciotomy
surgeries.description: Cutting the fascial sheath of a swollen limb to relieve the pressure inside the muscle compartment, restoring blood flow before the tissue dies.
steps: Make a long incision through the skin.
Retract the skin to expose the fascia.
Cut the fascia open along its length to release the pressure.
Cauterize the incision closed.

surgeries.name: Chest tube placement
surgeries.description: Opening the pleural space to vent trapped air, letting the collapsed lung re-expand.
steps: Incise through the skin below the armpit.
Retract the intercostal muscle.
Open the pleural space and release the trapped air.
Cauterize the incision closed.

surgeries.name: Lung tissue repair
surgeries.description: Opening the chest to mend torn or bruised lung tissue directly. Respiratory failure driven by the damaged lung recedes as it heals.
steps: Open the chest and retract the skin.
Saw through and retract the ribcage.
Suture the damaged lung.
Set the ribcage back together.
Cauterize the incision closed.

surgeries.name: Open cardiac repair
surgeries.description: Opening the chest to suture damaged heart muscle. Heart damage recedes as the muscle heals; follow-up care is still needed.
steps: Open the chest and retract the skin.
Saw through and retract the ribcage.
Suture the damaged cardiac tissue.
Set the ribcage back together.
Cauterize the incision closed.

surgeries.name: Necrotic organ resection
surgeries.description: Cutting dead tissue out of an internal organ before it spreads. Sutures don't touch necrosis; only resection removes it.
steps: Open the region and retract the tissue.
Where the organ is encased, saw through and retract the bone.
Resect the necrotic tissue from the organ.
Set any bone back together.
Close the region in layers.

surgeries.name: Craniotomy
surgeries.description: Opening the skull to drain a subdural bleed and relieve cranial pressure, then repairing the bruised brain tissue beneath. A brain that has already died does not recover.
steps: Open the scalp.
Cut into the skull with a circular saw and lift the bone flap.
Drain the bleed and relieve the pressure.
Suture the injured brain tissue.
Set the skull back in place.
Close the scalp.

surgeries.name: Exploratory laparotomy for bleeding
surgeries.description: Opening the abdomen to find and repair bleeding that imaging or pressure couldn't resolve.
steps: Make a midline abdominal incision.
Retract the abdominal wall.
Find the source of the bleeding and repair the vessel.
Close in layers.

surgeries.name: Retinal repair
surgeries.description: Opening the orbit to repair damaged eye tissue. Vision loss from the injured eye recedes as it heals.
steps: Open the skin around the eye.
Retract the lids and soft tissue.
Saw through and lift the orbital bone.
Suture the damaged eye.
Set the bone back in place.
Close the incision.

surgeries.name: Prosthetic maintenance
surgeries.description: Opening a prosthetic limb's maintenance hatch to weld dented plating, replace burned wiring and restore faulted components.
steps: Unscrew the maintenance hatch.
Pry the hatch open.
Weld the damaged plating and replace burned wiring.
Repair faulted internal components with nanopaste.
Close and secure the hatch.

spells.name: Audible Deception
spells.desc: Allows you to create a specific sound at a location of your choosing.
spells.enhancement_desc: An extremely loud bike horn sound that costs  large amount of energy and instability becomes available, which will deafen and stun all who are near the targeted tile, including yourself if unprotected.

spells.name: Blink
spells.desc: Force the target to teleport a short distance away.  This target could be anything from something lying on the ground, to someone trying to fight you, or even yourself.  Using this on someone next to you makes their potential distance after teleportation greater.  Self casting has the greatest potential for distance, as well as the cheapest cost.
spells.spell_power_desc: Blink distance is scaled up with more spell power.

spells.name: Condensation
spells.desc: This causes rapid formation of liquid at the target, causing floors to become wet, entities to be soaked, and fires to be extinguished.  You can also fill contains with water if they are targeted directly.
spells.enhancement_desc: Floors affected by condensation will also freeze.

spells.name: Control
spells.desc: This function allows you to exert control over simple-minded entities to an extent, such as spiders and carp.  Controlled entities will not be hostile towards you, and you may direct them to move to specific areas or to attack specific targets.  This function will have no effect on entities of higher intelligence, such as humans and similar alien species, as it's not true mind control, but merely pheromone synthesis for living animals, and electronic hacking for simple robots.  The green web around the entity is merely a hologram used to allow the user to know if the creature is safe or not.

spells.name: Illusion
spells.desc: Allows you to create and control a holographic illusion, that can take the form of most object or entities.
spells.enhancement_desc: Illusions will be made of hard light, allowing the interception of attacks, appearing more realistic.

spells.name: Oxygenate
spells.desc: This function creates oxygen at a location of your chosing.  If used on a humanoid entity, it heals oxygen deprivation.  If casted on the envirnment, air (oxygen and nitrogen) is moved from a distant location to your target.

spells.name: Radiance
spells.desc: Causes you to be very radiant, glowing brightly in visible light, thermal energy, and deadly ionizing radiation.  Note that this WILL affect you.
spells.spell_power_desc: Spell power increases the amount of radiation and heat radiated, as well as the radius.
spells.enhancement_desc: Radiation will not affect the caster or their allies.

spells.name: Resurrect
spells.desc: This function injects various regenetive medical compounds and nanomachines, in an effort to restart the body, however this must be done soon after they die, as this will have no effect on people who have died long ago.  It also doesn't resolve whatever caused them to die originally.

spells.name: Shared Burden
spells.desc: One of the few functions able to adjust instability, this allows you to take someone else's instability.
spells.spell_power_desc: Draws bonus instability from the target, with the bonus dissipating harmlessly, for 'free'.

spells.name: Targeting Matrix
spells.desc: Automatically targets and fires a ranged weapon or function at a non-friendly target near a targeted tile.  Each target assisted attack costs some energy and instability.

spells.name: Track
spells.desc: Acts as directional guidance towards an object that belongs to you or your team.  It can also point towards your allies.  Wonderful if you're worried someone will steal your valuables, like a certain shiny Scepter...
spells.enhancement_desc: You will be able to track most other entities in addition to your belongings and allies.

spells.name: Warp Strike
spells.desc: Teleports you next to your target, and attacks them with whatever is in your off-hand, spell or object.

spells.name: Corona
spells.desc: Causes the victim to glow very brightly, which while harmless in itself, makes it easier for them to be hit.  The bright glow also makes it very difficult to be stealthy.  The effect lasts for one minute.

spells.name: Haste
spells.desc: Allows the target to run at speeds that should not be possible for an ordinary being.  For five seconds, the target runs extremly fast, and cannot be slowed by any means.

spells.name: Mend Life
spells.desc: Heals minor wounds, such as cuts, bruises, burns, and other non-lifethreatening injuries.  Instability is split between the target and technomancer, if separate.  The function will end prematurely if the target is completely healthy, preventing further instability.

spells.name: Mend Synthetic
spells.desc: Repairs minor damage to prosthetics.  Instability is split between the target and technomancer, if separate.  The function will end prematurely if the target is completely healthy, preventing further instability.

spells.name: Purify
spells.desc: Clenses the body of harmful impurities, such as toxins, radiation, viruses, genetic damage, and such.  Instability is split between the target and technomancer, if separate.  The function will end prematurely if the target is completely healthy, preventing further instability.

spells.name: Repel Missiles
spells.desc: Places a repulsion field around you, which attempts to deflect incoming bullets and lasers, making them 45% less likely to hit you.  The field lasts for 10 minutes and can be granted to yourself or an ally.

spells.name: Beam
spells.desc: Fires a laser at your target.  Cheap, reliable, and a bit boring.

spells.name: Chain Lightning
spells.desc: This dangerous function shoots lightning that will strike someone, then bounce to a nearby person.  Be careful that it does not bounce to you.  The lighting prefers to bounce to people with the least resistance to electricity.  It will strike up to four targets, including yourself if conditions allow it to occur.  Lightning functions cannot miss due to distance.

spells.name: Force Missile
spells.desc: This fires a missile at your target.  It's cheap to use, however the projectile itself moves and impacts in such a way that armor designed to protect from blunt force will mitigate this function as well.

spells.name: Ionic Bolt
spells.desc: Shoots a bolt of ion energy at the target.  If it hits something, it will generally drain energy, corrupt electronics, or otherwise ruin complex machinery.

spells.name: Lesser Chain Lightning
spells.desc: This is very similar to the function Chain Lightning, however it is considerably less powerful.  As a result, it's a lot more economical in terms of energy cost, as well as instability generation.  Lightning functions cannot miss due to distance.

spells.name: Lightning Strike
spells.desc: This uses a hidden electrolaser, which creates a laser beam to ionize the enviroment, allowing for ideal conditions for a directed lightning strike to occur.  The lightning is very strong, however it requires a few seconds to prepare a strike.  Lightning functions cannot miss due to distance.

spells.name: Overload
spells.desc: Fires a bolt of highly unstable energy, that does damaged equal to 0.3% of the technomancer's current reserve of energy.  This energy pierces all known armor.  Energy cost is equal to 10% of maximum core charge.
spells.spell_power_desc: Increases damage dealt, up to a cap of 80 damage per shot.
spells.enhancement_desc: Will do damage equal to 0.4% of current energy.

spells.name: Darkness
spells.desc: Disrupts photons moving in a local area, causing darkness to shroud yourself or a position of your choosing.

spells.name: Fire Blast
spells.desc: Causes a disturbance on a targeted tile.  After two and a half seconds, it will explode in a small radius around it.  Be sure to not be close to the disturbance yourself.

spells.name: Summon Creature
spells.desc: Teleports a specific creature from their current location in the universe to the targeted tile, after a delay. The creature summoned can be chosen by using the ability in your hand. Available creatures are; mice, crabs, parrots, bats, goats, cats, corgis, spiders, and space carp. The creatures take a few moments to be teleported to the targeted tile. Note that the creatures summoned are not inherently loyal to the technomancer, and that the creatures will be hurt slightly from being teleported to you.
spells.spell_power_desc: The strength and endurance of the summoned creature will be greater.
spells.enhancement_desc: Summoned entities will never harm their summoner.

spells.name: Summon Monitor Ward
spells.desc: Teleports a prefabricated 'ward' drone to the target location, which will alert you when it sees entities moving around it, or when it is attacked. They can see for up to five meters. It can also see invisible entities, and forcefully decloak them if close enough.

spells.name: Abjuration
spells.desc: This ability attempts to send summoned or teleported entities or anomalies to the place from whence they came, or at least far away from the caster.  Failing that, it may inhibit those entities in some form.

spells.name: Apportation
spells.desc: This allows you to teleport objects into your hand, or to pull people towards you.  If they're close enough, the function will grab them automatically.

spells.name: Chroma
spells.desc: Creates light around you, or in a location of your choosing.  You can choose what color the light is.  This could be useful to trick someone into believing you're casting a different spell, or perhaps just for fun.

spells.name: Dispel
spells.desc: Ends most on-going effects caused by another Technomancer function on the target.  Useful if you are worried about hitting an ally with a deterimental function, if your opponent has similar capabilities to you, or if you're tired of Instability plaguing you.

spells.name: Energy Siphon
spells.desc: This creates a link to a target that drains electricity, converts it to energy that the Core can use, then absorbs it.  Every second, electricity is stolen until the link is broken by the target moving too far away, or having no more energy left.  Can drain from powercells, microbatteries, and other Cores.  The beam created by the siphoning is harmful to touch.
spells.spell_power_desc: Rate of siphoning is scaled up based on spell power.

spells.name: Flame Tongue
spells.desc: Using a miniturized flamethrower in your gloves, you can emit a flame strong enough to melt both your enemies and walls.

spells.name: Gambit
spells.desc: This function causes you to receive a random function, including those which you haven't purchased.
spells.spell_power_desc: Makes certain rare functions possible to acquire via Gambit which cannot be obtained otherwise, if above 100%.
spells.enhancement_desc: Instead of a purely random spell, it will give you a "random" spell.

spells.name: Instability Tap
spells.desc: Creates a large sum of energy (5,000 at normal spell power), at the cost of a very large amount of instability afflicting you.
spells.spell_power_desc: Amount of energy gained scaled with spell power.
spells.enhancement_desc: 50% more energy gained, 20% less instability gained.

spells.name: Mark
spells.desc: This function places a specific 'mark' beacon under you, which is used by the Recall function as a destination.  Note that using Mark again will move the destination instead of creating a second destination, and only one destination can exist, regardless of who casted Mark.

spells.name: Recall
spells.desc: This function teleports you to where you placed a mark using the Mark function.  Without the Mark function, this function is useless.  Note that teleporting takes three seconds.  Being incapacitated while teleporting will cancel it.
spells.enhancement_desc: Recall takes two seconds instead of three.

spells.name: Mend Internals
spells.desc: Greatly heals the target's wounds, both external and internal.  Restores internal organs to functioning states, even if robotic, reforms bones, patches internal bleeding, and restores missing blood.

spells.name: Passwall
spells.desc: An uncommon function that allows the user to phase through matter (usually walls) in order to enter or exit a room.  Be careful you don't pass into somewhere dangerous.

spells.name: Phase Shift
spells.desc: Hides you in the safest possible place, where no harm can come to you.  Unfortunately, a prolonged stay inside the rift you create will afflict you with instability.

spells.name: Reflect
spells.desc: Emits a protective shield fron your hand in front of you, which will reflect one attack back at the attacker.

spells.name: Shield
spells.desc: Emits a protective shield fron your hand in front of you, which will protect you from almost anything able to harm you, so long as you can power it.  Stronger attacks blocked cost more energy to sustain.  Note that holding two shields will make blocking more energy efficent.
spells.enhancement_desc: Blocking is twice as efficent in terms of energy cost per hit.

spells.name: Restoration Aura
spells.desc: Heals you and your allies (or everyone, if you want) of trauma and burns slowly, as long as they remain within four meters.
spells.spell_power_desc: Increases the radius and healing amount of the aura.

spells.name: Fire Storm
spells.desc: This causes everyone within four meters of you to heat up, eventually burning to death if they remain for too long.  This does not affect you or your allies.  It also causes a large amount of fire to erupt around you, however the main threat is still the heating up.
spells.spell_power_desc: Radius, heat rate, heat capacity, and amount of fires made increased.
spells.enhancement_desc: Increased heat generation, more fires, and higher temperature cap.

spells.name: Chilling Aura
spells.desc: Lowers the core body temperature of everyone around you (except for your friends), causing them to become very slow if they stay within four meters of you.
spells.spell_power_desc: Radius and rate of cooling are scaled.
spells.enhancement_desc: Will make nearby entities even slower.

spells.name: Electric Aura
spells.desc: Repeatively electrocutes enemies within four meters of you, as well as nearby electronics.
spells.enhancement_desc: Aura does twice as much damage.

spells.name: Degen Aura
spells.desc: Destabalizes your enemies, breaking their elements down to their basic levels, slowly killing them from the inside. For each person within fourteen meters of you, they suffer 1% of their current health every second. Your allies are unharmed.

spells.name: Destablize
spells.desc: Creates an unstable disturbance at the targeted tile, which will afflict anyone nearby with instability who remains nearby.  This can affect you and your allies as well.  The disturbance lasts for twenty seconds.

spells.name: Pulsar
spells.desc: Emits electronic pulses to destroy, disable, or otherwise harm devices and machines.  Be sure to not hit yourself with this.

equipment.name: Manipulation Core
equipment.desc:
The default core that you most likely already have. This is here in-case you change your mind after buying another core, don't forget to refund the old core.
Capacity: 10k
Recharge: 50/s
Instability Modifier: 80%
Energy Cost Modifier: 100%
Spell Power: 100%

equipment.name: Rapid Core
equipment.desc:
A core optimized for passive regeneration, however at the cost of capacity. Has a capacity of 7,000 units of energy, and recharges at a rate of 70 units. Complex gravatics and force manipulation allows the wearer to also run slightly faster.
Capacity: 7k
Recharge: 70/s
Instability Modifier: 90%
Energy Cost Modifier: 100%
Spell Power: 100%

equipment.name: Bulky Core
equipment.desc:
This core has very large capacitors, however it also has a subpar fractal reactor. The user is recommended to purchase one or more energy-generating Functions as well if using this core. The intense weight of the core unfortunately can cause the wear to move slightly slower, and the closeness of the capacitors causes a slight increase in incoming instability.
Capacity: 20k
Recharge: 25/s
Instability Modifier: 100%
Energy Cost Modifier: 100%
Spell Power: 140%

equipment.name: Unstable Core
equipment.desc:
This core feeds off unstable energies around the user in addition to a fractal reactor. This means that it performs better as the user has more instability, which could prove dangerous to the inexperienced or unprepared. The rate of recharging increases as the user accumulates more instability, eventually exceeding even the rapid core in regen speed, at a huge risk.
Capacity: 13k
Recharge: 35/s to 110/s+
Instability Modifier: 130%
Energy Cost Modifier: 70%
Spell Power: 110%

equipment.name: Recycling Core
equipment.desc:
This core is optimized for energy efficency, being able to sometimes recover energy that would have been lost with other cores. Each time energy is spent, there is a 30% chance of recovering half of what was spent.
Capacity: 12k
Recharge: 40/s
Instability Modifier: 60%
Energy Cost Modifier: 80%
Spell Power: 100%

equipment.name: Summoning Core
equipment.desc:
A unique type of core, this one sacrifices other characteristics in order to optimize it for the purposes teleporting entities from vast distances, and keeping them there. Wearers of this core can maintain up to 40 summons at once, and the energy demand for maintaining summons is severely reduced.
Capacity: 8k
Recharge: 35/s
Instability Modifier: 120%
Energy Cost Modifier: 100%
Spell Power: 120%

equipment.name: Safety Core
equipment.desc:
This core is designed so that the wearer suffers almost no instability. It unfortunately comes at a cost of subpar ratings for everything else.
Capacity: 7k
Recharge: 30/s
Instability Modifier: 30%
Energy Cost Modifier: 100%
Spell Power: 70%

equipment.name: Overcharged Core
equipment.desc:
A core that was created in order to get the most power out of functions. It does this by shoving the most power into those functions, so it is the opposite of energy efficent, however the enhancement of functions is second to none for other cores.
Capacity: 15k (effectively 7.5k)
Recharge: 40/s
Instability Modifier: 110%
Energy Cost Modifier: 200%
Spell Power: 175%

equipment.name: Hypo Belt
equipment.desc: A medical belt designed to carry autoinjectors and other medical equipment.  Comes with one of each hypo.

equipment.name: Belt of Holding
equipment.desc: A belt with a literal pocket which opens to a localized pocket of 'Blue-Space', allowing for more storage.  The nature of the pocket allows for storage of larger objects than what is typical for other belts, and in larger quanities.  It will also help keep your pants on.

equipment.name: Thermoncle
equipment.desc: A fancy monocle with a thermal optics lens installed.  Allows you to see people across walls.

equipment.name: Night Vision Goggles
equipment.desc: Strategical goggles which will allow the wearer to see in the dark.  Perfect for the sneaky type, just get rid of the lights first.

equipment.name: Omnisight Scanner
equipment.desc: A very rare scanner worn on the face, which allows the wearer to see nearly anything across walls.

equipment.name: Medical HUD
equipment.desc: A commonly available HUD for medical professionals, which displays how healthy an individual is.  Recommended for support-based apprentices!

equipment.name: Scepter of Empowerment
equipment.desc: A gem sometimes found in the depths of asteroids makes up the basis for this device.  Energy is channeled into it from the Core and the user, causing many functions to be enhanced in various ways, so long as it is held in the off-hand.  Be careful not to lose this!

equipment.name: Spyglass
equipment.desc: A mundane spyglass, it may prove useful to those who wish to scout ahead, or fight from an extreme range.

equipment.name: Boots of Speed
equipment.desc: What appears to be an ordinary pair of boots, is actually a bit more useful than that.  These will help against slipping on flat surfaces, and will make you run a bit faster than if you had normal shoes or boots on.

equipment.name: Gloves of Regeneration
equipment.desc: It's a pair of black gloves, with a hypodermic needle on the insides, and a small storage of a secret blend of chemicals designed to be slowly fed into a living person's system, increasing their metabolism greatly, resulting in accelerated healing.  A side effect of this healing is that the wearer will generally get hungry a lot faster.  Sliding the gloves on and off also hurts a lot.  As a bonus, the gloves are more resistant to the elements than most.  It should be noted that synthetics will have little use for these.

equipment.name: Personal Shield Projector
equipment.desc: This state-of-the-art technology uses the bleeding edge of energy distribution and field projection to provide a personal shield around you, which can diffuse laser beams and reduce the velocity of bullets and close quarters weapons, reducing their potential for harm severely.  All of this comes at a cost of of requiring a large amount of energy, of which your Core can provide.  When you are struck by something, the shield will block 75% of the damage, deducting energy proportional to the amount of force that was inflicted.  Armor penetration has no effect on the shield's ability to protect you from harm, however the shield will fail if the energy supply cannot meet demand.

equipment.name: Tesla Armor
equipment.desc: This piece of armor offers a retaliation-based defense.  When the armor is 'ready', it will completely protect you from the next attack you suffer, and strike the attacker with a strong bolt of lightning, provided they are close enough.  This effect requires fifteen seconds to recharge.  If you are attacked while this is recharging, a weaker lightning bolt is sent out, however you won't be protected from the person beating you.

consumables.name: Trauma Hypo
consumables.desc: A extended capacity hypo which can treat blunt trauma.

consumables.name: Burn Hypo
consumables.desc: A extended capacity hypo which can treat severe burns.

consumables.name: Toxin Hypo
consumables.desc: A extended capacity hypo which can treat various toxins.

consumables.name: Oxy Hypo
consumables.desc: A extended capacity hypo which can treat oxygen deprivation.

consumables.name: Purity Hypo
consumables.desc: A extended capacity hypo which can remove various inpurities in the system such as viruses, infections, radiation, and genetic problems.

consumables.name: Pain Hypo
consumables.desc: A extended capacity hypo which contains potent painkillers.

consumables.name: Organ Hypo
consumables.desc: A extended capacity hypo which is designed to fix internal organ problems.

consumables.name: Combat Hypo
consumables.desc: A extended capacity hypo containing a dangerous cocktail of various combat stims.

consumables.name: Freedom Implant
consumables.desc: A hidden implant which allows one to escape bindings such as handcuffs.

consumables.name: Explosive Implant
consumables.desc: A hidden implant which will explode if it hears a passphrase.

consumables.name: Disposable Teleporter
consumables.desc: An ultra-safe teleportation device that can directly teleport you to a number of locations at minimal risk, however it has a limited amount of charges.

assistance.name: Friendly Apprentice
assistance.desc: A one-time use teleporter that sends a less powerful manipulator of space to you, who will do their best to protect and serve you.  They get their own catalog and can buy spells for themselves, however they have a smaller pool to buy with.  If you are unable to receive an apprentice, the teleporter can be refunded like most equipment by sliding it into the catalog.  Note that apprentices cannot purchase more apprentices.

items.name: photovoltaic cell (tiny)
items.desc: It's a very tiny solar cell, generally used in calculators.

items.name: photovoltaic cell (small)

items.name: photovoltaic cell (standard)

items.name: photovoltaic cell (large)
items.desc: It's a large solar cell, generally used en masse to store power for later use.

items.desc: This tiny circuit will send a pulse right after device is turned on, or when power is restored.

items.name: metabolic siphon
items.desc: A complicated piece of technology which converts bodily nutriments of a host into electricity.

items.name: internal energy siphon
items.desc: A small circuit designed to be connected to an internal power wire inside a synthetic entity.

items.name: tesla power relay
items.desc: A seemingly enigmatic device which connects to nearby APCs wirelessly and draws power from them.

items.name: large tesla power relay
items.desc: A seemingly enigmatic device which connects to nearby APCs wirelessly and draws power from them, now in industiral size!

items.name: fuel cell
items.desc: Produces electricity from chemicals.

items.name: power network interface

items.name: rot13 circuit
